findings.label: validation
findings.failure_mode: A pack file with all five correctly-spelled section headings but a structural violation the validator hasn't implemented yet (unclosed wiring fence, unescaped pipe in a table cell, malformed bash in Brief probes, an unquoted citation, or a label not in the closed list) passes validate-pack.sh with exit 0 instead of being rejected. The co-shipped spec tests/run.sh expects exit 1 for exactly these five malformed fixtures, so running tests/run.sh fails on all five.
evidence: .claude/skills/pr-review/scripts/validate-pack.sh:24-26 — only check performed is exact-match grep over the five heading strings
.claude/skills/pr-review/scripts/validate-pack.sh:28-30 — TODO comment defers wiring-fence, pipe-in-cell, label-membership, brief-syntax, and citation-quoting checks
tests/packs/bad-wiring-unfenced.md:9-12 — all five headings present verbatim; only defect is the unterminated fence after '## Wiring files'
tests/run.sh:323 — check "bad-wiring-unfenced.md" 1 expects the validator to reject this fixture
bash validate-pack.sh tests/packs/bad-wiring-unfenced.md exits 0, so tests/run.sh reports FAIL (exit 0, want 1) — invalid pack silently accepted

findings.label: duplication
findings.failure_mode: The five required pack-section headings and the exact-match grep check against them are re-declared independently here instead of reusing the identical list already in build-artifacts.sh; a future edit to the pack format contract applied to only one of the two copies makes build-artifacts.sh (warn-and-continue) and validate-pack.sh (hard-fail) disagree on whether the same pack is valid.
evidence: .claude/skills/pr-review/scripts/build-artifacts.sh:52 — for h in "## Stack scope prefixes" ... ; do (original five-heading list)
build-artifacts.sh:58 — echo "warning: domain pack is missing ..." (non-blocking failure path)
validate-pack.sh:18 — for h in "## Stack scope prefixes" ... ; do (independent re-declaration of the same list)
validate-pack.sh:19 — grep -qxF "$h" "$PACK" || fail ... (blocking failure path, own copy of the rule)
